clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-226], sentences 1-2: "Grid Worm does not constrain a newly fired tear immediately."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:812-828 fires a (3,4) tear and requires an axis-locked velocity two update frames later.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-226], sentence 3: "its first direction can disagree with the direction the character is facing"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:821-831 compares the velocity with player:GetHeadDirection(). Only the idle DOWN heading is exercised (head=3 in both baseline logs).

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-226], sentence 4: "Tears that hit a wall also invert their velocity without leaving the collision tile, so they can oscillate in place instead of rebounding cleanly."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:889-941. Asserted, but with an implementation-shaped threshold: see known_issues[0].

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-226], last sentence: "Keep the existing later random-turn cadence; fixing the opening direction must not make those periodic turns start sooner." (also catalog requirement 2)
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:836-888 follows twelve tears for about twelve frames and requires every direction to stay unchanged (dot > 0.99). Passes in the unchanged starter.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-239]: "The trinket may clear room obstacles, but the room boundary and its door must remain intact."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/secret-suite/main.lua:104-120 only requires walls >= 10 and doors >= 1 in s.secret.1. The reference keeps 43 wall tiles and the starter 1, so a repair that still deletes three quarters of the boundary would pass.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-251]: "Enemies or pickups that appear later on that same floor render normally, even though the broken-world effect is meant to persist until the next floor"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:942-961 drops the trinket, spawns a Gaper and requires its sprite colour to be black four frames later. Pickups and the tear-doubling half of the effect are not checked.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-251], same sentence: "... meant to persist until the next floor and reset there."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:979-993 spawns a Gaper after `stage 1` and requires it NOT to be black. It passes trivially in the starter (the effect already ends at the drop) and becomes discriminating once EX-251 is repaired; control compat-negative-broken-glasses-floor-reset shows that.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-184]: "The Forbidden Fruit's earned damage disappears if the item is removed or rerolled."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:267-284 uses the item once, removes it with RemoveCollectible, re-evaluates the damage cache and requires the damage to stay within 0.05 of the held value. clauses.note: Runtime fact added in catalog 5.0.0; no case asserts it on its own.

known_issues: Over-constraining: grid_worm_bounce (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:929-932) requires the tear to be >= 35 units from the struck wall tile on the FIRST frame on which its velocity is seen reversed. Both baselines reverse on the same frame (age=2); the starter is then at 30.0 and the reference at 40.0, only because gold adds `Position = Position + Velocity` in the reversal frame. A repair that reverses once per impact and lets the tear fly clear on the following frames (30, 40, 50 ...) rebounds cleanly and never oscillates, yet is measured at 30 and rejected. Control alternative-strict-reading demonstrates this.

Order dependence: the thirty main-suite cases share one run and one player (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:264-1009). State leaks forward (Forbidden Fruit's +0.99 damage is part of every later damage figure; Mutant Clover is silently replaced by Anamnesis before its reset guard; a pcall failure in any step emits GCB_FATAL and leaves every later case unobserved).

Shared game-log markers (private NOTES.md, Verifier design): results are parsed from unauthenticated `[GCB_CASE]` lines written through Isaac.DebugString into the same log the submission can write to, so outcomes are only meaningful under the honest-code assumption.

Process coupling: the secret-room process runs with continued=true as player_type=18 (James), inheriting the James process's run from Steam's in-memory cache (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/test.sh:85-108). apocryphon_stats and blue_moon are therefore measured on James, who already owns The Apocryphon.

Launch harness: this task runs the frozen composite's three suites and test.sh unchanged, but the Hub mounts the task's own tests/run-game.sh over the image's copy. That script queues the launch request as soon as the offline Steam client proper is up, repeats an ignored request once, replaces a client that takes none (up to four starts per game process), and allows longer wall-clock budgets. It decides no case. The image's launch sequence left game processes unstarted on the congested host on 2026-09-23 (UTC); see NOTES.md.
